This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera.
The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia.

There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95.

Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.
The only other November tornado recorded was in 1989.Severe storms have also resulted in tornadoes in Argentina as well as large hailstones.
A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the central Córdoba province on Friday, bringing hailstones up to the size of a baseball (about 7.5cm in diameter).
Parts of the province recorded up to 73mm of rainfall in just six hours early on Saturday.
Such storms are common at this time of year.
Water vapour from the Amazon meeting the Andes quickly condenses, resulting in massive cloud formations often associated with heavy downpours, lightning, tornadoes and large hailstones.

facts: Today, the Reserve Bank released the second edition of its biennial Report titled “Finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions”.
The theme of this edition is ‘Local Finances and Capacity Building in Rural India’.

Drawing upon a balanced panel of 2.25 lakh Gram Panchayats for the period 2022-23 to 2024-25, the Report presents an assessment of their finances and their role in achieving sustainable and inclusive rural socio-economic development.

Highlights:                  Gram Panchayat finances strengthened during 2022-23 and 2023-24; they, however, remain dependent on intergovernmental transfers, accounting for about 90 per cent of total receipts, while own source revenues (OSR) accounted for a modest share of about 10 per cent, predominantly driven by non-tax receipts such as interest receipts, Panchayati Raj programme funds and user charges.

Expenditure patterns primarily reflected both the mandates of the Fifteenth Finance Commission and convergence with national schemes/missions, with water supply and sanitation accounting for the largest share (about 40 per cent) of total expenditure.
While notable progress has been made in rural connectivity, electrification, water supply, sanitation and community assets, inter-State disparities persist in access, quality and functionality.
This Report has been prepared in the Division of Local Finances of the Department of Economic and Policy Research.
The current edition, along with the previous edition of the Report, is available on the Reserve Bank’s website (www.rbi.org.in).
(Brij Raj)               Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1524
analysisOrUncertainties: As some large Gram Panchayats transition to small urban local bodies or Town Panchayats, functional responsibilities may expand faster than fiscal and administrative preparedness, requiring transitional fiscal support and administrative capacity building alongside a calibrated strengthening of OSR through improved collection efficiency and rationalised property taxes and license fees.

Feedback and comments to help improve the analytical and informational content of the Report may be sent to the Director, Division of Local Finances, Department of Economic and Policy Research, Amar Building (6th Floor), Reserve Bank of India, Sir Pherozshah Mehta Road, Mumbai – 400 001 or through e-mail.

facts: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 17, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹7.50 lakh (Rupees Seven Lakh Fifty Thousand only) on Fusion Finance Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of directions issued by RBI on ‘Know Your Customer (KYC)’ and ‘Internal Ombudsman’.
This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under section 58G(1)(b) read with section 58B(5)(aa) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its financial position as on March 31, 2026.

Based on the supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for failure to comply with the RBI directions.

After considering the company's reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty:                  The company failed to obtain PAN or equivalent e-document thereof or Form 60 from customers, while establishing an account-based relationship with those customers; and,                    The company failed to escalate the partly or wholly rejected complaints to the Internal Ombudsman for a final decision within the prescribed time.
This action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers.
(Brij Raj)                 Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1537
analysisOrUncertainties: Further, imposition of this monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company.

facts: The following State Governments have announced the conversion/switch of their securities through auction for an aggregate amount of ₹10,800 crore (face value).
The auction will be a multiple-price based auction, i.e., successful bids will get accepted at their respective quoted prices for the source and destination securities.
Bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the e-Kuber platform on November 26, 2026 (Thursday) between 10:30 AM and 11:30 AM.
The result of the auction will be announced on the same day and settlement will take place on November 27, 2026 (Friday).
Purchase marginally higher than the notified amount due to rounding-off effect.
Accept or reject any or all the offers either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.
Operational guidelines for switch transactions and other details are given in the Annex.

Ajit Prasad                  Deputy General Manager        (Communications)          Press Release: 2026-2027/1539            Annex      Operational Guidelines for Switch/Conversion Transactions of State Government Securities      Switch module on e-Kuber      1.
The market participants can bid in the switch auction through the Switch Transaction module provided in the e-Kuber portal.
Bidding in a switch transaction      2.

Bidding in the auction implies that the market participants agree to sell the source security/ies to the respective State Government and simultaneously agree to buy the destination security from the same State Government at their respective quoted prices.
Placing of bids      3.
Each bid should specify the following details:                        Amount of the source security (Face Value) that the participants are willing to sell.
Price of the source security (expressed up to two decimal places).
Choice of destination security and the price of the destination security (expressed up to two decimal places), at which the participants are willing to buy the destination security.

The participants can choose to bid for any/all the destination security/ies, but the aggregate amount of bids for the source security should not exceed their holdings of the source security in face value terms.
Minimum Bid size      5.
Minimum bid size would be ₹10,000 and in multiples of ₹10,000 thereafter.
The participants are allowed to submit multiple bids.
However, the aggregate amount of bids submitted should not exceed the notified amount of source security/basket of source securities in the auction.
Price of source security      6.
The price of the source security quoted must be equal to the FBIL closing price of the source security as on the previous working day.
Bids for source security not as per the price mentioned above will be rejected.
Price of destination security      8.
Method of auction      9.
The auction will be a multiple-price based auction, i.e.
successful bids will get accepted at their respective quoted prices for the source and destination securities.
Auction decision      10.
The auction cut-off will be decided based on the price of the destination security/ies.
Successful bidders are those who have placed their bids at or above the cut-off price.
All bids lower than the cut-off price will be rejected.
There will be provision of pro-rata allotment, should there be more than one successful bid at the cut-off price.
Amount of destination security and dealing in odd amounts during switch auction      13.
The switch ratio, which is the ratio of the price of the source security to the price of the destination security, would be rounded off at 8 decimal places.
The amount of destination security to be issued for each successful bid will be computed by multiplying the allotted amount (FV) of the source security with the rounded-off switch ratio.
The amount of destination security (FV) would be rounded-off to the nearest lower value in multiples of ₹10,000.

The odd amount of destination securities (less than ₹10,000) which has been rounded-off, would be notionally allotted and bought back from the bidders at the quoted bid price of the destination security.

The net cash consideration to be paid to the bidder for such odd amounts would be the clean price of these securities (as the accrued interest received during notional allotment and paid during notional buyback offset each other).
Fund settlement      16.

Though the conversion would be broadly cash neutral, there will be fund settlement for the net accrued interest (accrued interest for the source security FV – accrued interest for the destination security FV) for each bid.
Cash consideration (due to rounding-off of face value of destination security) computed for each bid would be added to the net accrued interest.
Accordingly, fund settlement will be done for the final amount (Net accrued interest + cash consideration) for each bid.

Note: An illustration for the calculation of cash consideration due to rounding-off of destination security face value is as given below:                       Amount of Source Security (FV)          ₹10,00,00,000.00                          Price of Source Security           ₹97.50                          Price of Destination Security           ₹99.20                          Switch Ratio (rounded-off at 8 decimals)          0.98286290                          Destination Security FV before rounding off           ₹9,82,86,290.00                           Destination Security FV re-issued after rounding-off           ₹9,82,80,000.00                           Odd amount of rounded-off destination security (FV)          ₹6290.00                           Cash consideration due to rounding off (Clean Price calculated at the quoted price of destination security)           ₹6240.00                     17.
The settlement of the auction would be held on T+1 basis.
Help Desk      18.
In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 22705125).

Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline.
Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday.

The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night.
Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches.
These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days.
Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento.
Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California.
By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

facts: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 17, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹7.50 lakh (Rupees Seven Lakh Fifty Thousand only) on Fusion Finance Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of directions issued by RBI on ‘Know Your Customer (KYC)’ and ‘Internal Ombudsman’.
This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under section 58G(1)(b) read with section 58B(5)(aa) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its financial position as on March 31, 2026.

Based on the supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for failure to comply with the RBI directions.

After considering the company's reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty:                  The company failed to obtain PAN or equivalent e-document thereof or Form 60 from customers, while establishing an account-based relationship with those customers; and,                    The company failed to escalate the partly or wholly rejected complaints to the Internal Ombudsman for a final decision within the prescribed time.
This action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers.

facts: The following State Governments have announced the conversion/switch of their securities through auction for an aggregate amount of ₹10,800 crore (face value).
The auction will be a multiple-price based auction, i.e., successful bids will get accepted at their respective quoted prices for the source and destination securities.
Bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the e-Kuber platform on November 26, 2026 (Thursday) between 10:30 AM and 11:30 AM.
The result of the auction will be announced on the same day and settlement will take place on November 27, 2026 (Friday).
Purchase marginally higher than the notified amount due to rounding-off effect.
Accept or reject any or all the offers either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.
Operational guidelines for switch transactions and other details are given in the Annex.

Ajit Prasad                  Deputy General Manager        (Communications)          Press Release: 2026-2027/1539            Annex      Operational Guidelines for Switch/Conversion Transactions of State Government Securities      Switch module on e-Kuber      1.
The market participants can bid in the switch auction through the Switch Transaction module provided in the e-Kuber portal.
Bidding in a switch transaction      2.

Bidding in the auction implies that the market participants agree to sell the source security/ies to the respective State Government and simultaneously agree to buy the destination security from the same State Government at their respective quoted prices.
Placing of bids      3.
Each bid should specify the following details:                        Amount of the source security (Face Value) that the participants are willing to sell.
Price of the source security (expressed up to two decimal places).
Choice of destination security and the price of the destination security (expressed up to two decimal places), at which the participants are willing to buy the destination security.

The participants can choose to bid for any/all the destination security/ies, but the aggregate amount of bids for the source security should not exceed their holdings of the source security in face value terms.
Minimum Bid size      5.
Minimum bid size would be ₹10,000 and in multiples of ₹10,000 thereafter.
The participants are allowed to submit multiple bids.
However, the aggregate amount of bids submitted should not exceed the notified amount of source security/basket of source securities in the auction.
Price of source security      6.
The price of the source security quoted must be equal to the FBIL closing price of the source security as on the previous working day.
Bids for source security not as per the price mentioned above will be rejected.
Price of destination security      8.
Method of auction      9.
The auction will be a multiple-price based auction, i.e.
successful bids will get accepted at their respective quoted prices for the source and destination securities.
Auction decision      10.
The auction cut-off will be decided based on the price of the destination security/ies.
Successful bidders are those who have placed their bids at or above the cut-off price.
All bids lower than the cut-off price will be rejected.
There will be provision of pro-rata allotment, should there be more than one successful bid at the cut-off price.
Amount of destination security and dealing in odd amounts during switch auction      13.
The switch ratio, which is the ratio of the price of the source security to the price of the destination security, would be rounded off at 8 decimal places.
The amount of destination security to be issued for each successful bid will be computed by multiplying the allotted amount (FV) of the source security with the rounded-off switch ratio.
The amount of destination security (FV) would be rounded-off to the nearest lower value in multiples of ₹10,000.

The odd amount of destination securities (less than ₹10,000) which has been rounded-off, would be notionally allotted and bought back from the bidders at the quoted bid price of the destination security.

The net cash consideration to be paid to the bidder for such odd amounts would be the clean price of these securities (as the accrued interest received during notional allotment and paid during notional buyback offset each other).
Fund settlement      16.

Though the conversion would be broadly cash neutral, there will be fund settlement for the net accrued interest (accrued interest for the source security FV – accrued interest for the destination security FV) for each bid.
Cash consideration (due to rounding-off of face value of destination security) computed for each bid would be added to the net accrued interest.
Accordingly, fund settlement will be done for the final amount (Net accrued interest + cash consideration) for each bid.

Note: An illustration for the calculation of cash consideration due to rounding-off of destination security face value is as given below:                       Amount of Source Security (FV)          ₹10,00,00,000.00                          Price of Source Security           ₹97.50                          Price of Destination Security           ₹99.20                          Switch Ratio (rounded-off at 8 decimals)          0.98286290                          Destination Security FV before rounding off           ₹9,82,86,290.00                           Destination Security FV re-issued after rounding-off           ₹9,82,80,000.00                           Odd amount of rounded-off destination security (FV)          ₹6290.00                           Cash consideration due to rounding off (Clean Price calculated at the quoted price of destination security)           ₹6240.00                     17.
The settlement of the auction would be held on T+1 basis.
Help Desk      18.
In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 22705125).

statesAndRegional.whyItMatters: Represents a key governance, legislative, or public policy milestone with direct outcomes for citizens and state administrations across India.
facts: The Foreign Exchange Management (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2015 were superseded by the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026, which were issued on January 13, 2026, and became effective from October 01, 2026.

The new regulations are principle based; intended to promote ease of doing business, especially for small exporters and importers; and empower Authorised Dealers to provide quicker and more efficient service to their customers.

Based on subsequent feedback received from stakeholders, the Reserve Bank has issued Amendment Regulations to Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 that were notified on November 02, 2026, and came into effect, retrospectively, from October 01, 2026.

In this regard, to facilitate better understanding of the new trade regulations by the exporters/importers and other stakeholders, the Reserve Bank has placed a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 on its website.
(Brij Raj)               Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1531

Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday.

The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night.
Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches.
These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days.
Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento.
Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California.
By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

facts: State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank continue to be identified as Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) under the same bucketing structure as in the 2025 list of D-SIBs.
The additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) requirement for these D-SIBs will be in addition to the capital conservation buffer.

The list of D-SIBs is as follows:                        Bucket          Banks          Additional Common Equity Tier 1 requirement as a percentage of Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs)                          5          -          1%                          4          State Bank of India          0.80%                          3          -          0.60%                          2          HDFC Bank          0.40%                          1          ICICI Bank          0.20%              Background:The Reserve Bank had issued the Framework for dealing with Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) on July 22, 2014, which was subsequently updated on December 28, 2023.

The D-SIB framework requires the Reserve Bank to disclose the names of banks designated as D-SIBs starting from 2015 and place these banks in appropriate buckets depending upon their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs).
Based on the bucket in which a D-SIB is placed, an additional common equity requirement has to be applied to it.

In case a foreign bank having branch presence in India is a Global Systemically Important Bank (G-SIB), it has to maintain additional CET1 capital surcharge in India as applicable to it as a G-SIB, proportionate to its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs) in India, i.e., additional CET1 buffer prescribed by the home regulator (amount) multiplied by India RWA as per consolidated global Group books divided by total consolidated global Group RWA.The Reserve Bank had announced SBI and ICICI Bank as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016 while HDFC Bank was classified as D-SIB in 2017 along with SBI and ICICI Bank.
The current update is based on the data collected from banks as on March 31, 2026.(Brij Raj)             Chief General ManagerPress Release: 2026-2027/1547

GoI will have the option to retain additional subscription up to ₹2,000 crore against each security mentioned above.
The securities will be sold through Reserve Bank of India Mumbai Office, Fort, Mumbai–400001.
The sale will be subject to the terms and conditions spelt out in the ‘Specific Notification’ mentioned above and the General Notification F.No.4(2)–B(W&M)/2018, dated March 26, 2025.
The auction will be conducted using multiple price method.
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system) on November 27, 2026 (Friday).
The non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m.
and the competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m.
The result will be announced on the same day and payment by successful bidders will have to be made on November 30, 2026 (Monday).
Bids for underwriting of the Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) portion can be submitted by ‘Primary Dealers’ from 09:00 a.m.
up to 09:30 a.m.
on November 27, 2026 (Friday) on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading for a period commencing from November 25, 2026 – November 27, 2026.
Operational guidelines for Government of India dated securities auction and other details are given in the Annex.
Ajit Prasad                  Deputy General Manager      (Communications)          Press Release: 2026-2027/1551ANNEX      Type of Auction      1.
For multiple price-based auction, successful bids will get accepted at the respective quoted yield/price for the security.
For uniform price-based auction, bids will get accepted at the cut off yield/price accepted in the auction.
The auction will be yield based for new security and price based for securities which are re-issued.
In case of a Floating Rate Bonds (FRB), the auction will be spread-based for new security and price based for securities which are reissued.
At the time of placing bids for new FRB, the spread should be quoted in percentage terms.
Minimum Bid Size      4.
The securities will be issued for a minimum amount of ₹10,000/- (nominal) and in multiples of ₹10,000/- thereafter.
Non-Competitive Segment      5.

In all the auctions, Government security up to 5% of the notified amount for sale of individual security will be allotted to the eligible individuals and institutions under the Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility in the Auctions of Government Securities.
Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).

Each bank or Primary Dealer (PD) on the basis of firm orders received from their constituents will submit a single consolidated non-competitive bid for individual security on behalf of its constituents in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
Allotment under the non-competitive segment will be at the weighted average rate of yield/price of the successful bids that will emerge in the auction on the basis of the competitive bidding.
Submission of Bids      8.
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
Bids in physical form will not be accepted except in extraordinary circumstances.
Business Continuity Plan (BCP)-IT failure      10.
Only in the event of system failure, physical bids will be accepted.

Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office, Mumbai through (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form which can be obtained from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.
In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).
Multiple Bids      13.
An investor can submit more than one competitive bid in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
The aggregate amount of bids submitted by an investor in an auction should not exceed the notified amount of auction.
Decision Making Process      15.
On the basis of bids received, the Reserve Bank will determine the minimum price/maximum yield up to which tenders for purchase of Government Security will be accepted at the auctions.
Bids quoted at rates lower than the minimum price/higher than the maximum yield determined by the Reserve Bank of India will be rejected.
Reserve Bank of India will have the full discretion to accept or reject any or all bids either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.
Issue of Securities      18.

Issue of securities to the successful bidders will be by credit to Subsidiary General Ledger Account (SGL) or to Constituents’ Subsidiary General Ledger Account (CSGL), maintained with Reserve Bank of India.
Periodicity of Interest Payment      19.
Interest on the Government Security will generally be paid half-yearly other than in case of securities with non-standard maturities.
The exact periodicity of coupon payment is invariably mentioned in the specific notification for the issue of security.
Underwriting of the Government Securities      20.

The underwriting of the Government Securities under auctions by the ‘Primary Dealers’ will be as per the “Revised Scheme of Underwriting Commitment and Liquidity Support” announced by the Reserve Bank vide circular RBI/2007-08/186 dated November 14, 2007 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for Repurchase Transactions (Repo)      21.

The securities will be eligible for Repurchase Transactions (Repo) as per the conditions mentioned in Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Repurchase Transactions (Repo)) Directions, 2025 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for ‘When Issued’ Trading      22.

The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading in accordance with the guidelines on ‘When Issued transactions in Central Government Securities’ issued by the Reserve Bank of India vide circular No.
RBI/2018-19/25 dated July 24, 2018 as amended from time to time.
Investment by Non-Residents    23.

Investments by Non-Residents are subject to the guidelines on ‘Fully Accessible Route’ for Investment by Non-residents in Government Securities and other related guidelines as issued by the Reserve Bank from time to time.

facts: As part of the Reserve Bank’s ongoing engagement with regulated entities, the Governor, Reserve Bank of India, today met in Mumbai with the Managing Directors and Chief Executive Officers (MDs & CEOs) of select Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), including Government NBFCs, Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) and Microfinance Institutions.
Representatives of Sa-Dhan, the Micro Finance Institutions Network (MFIN) and the Finance Industry Development Council (FIDC) also participated.
Deputy Governors Shri Swaminathan J., Dr Poonam Gupta, Shri S.
Murmu and Shri Rohit Jain attended the meeting, along with other senior officers of the Reserve Bank.
The MD & CEO of the National Housing Bank also participated.
The Governor acknowledged the role of NBFCs and HFCs in supporting economic activity by widening access to credit.
He emphasised the need for responsible and sustainable credit growth and urged NBFCs to put customers first as they expand their business.
He highlighted the importance of quality service, effective grievance redressal and fair recovery practices.
He also encouraged NBFCs to use the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) for customer onboarding and to keep customer records in the registry up to date to improve customer convenience.

The Governor urged participants to strengthen their cybersecurity infrastructure and adopt a comprehensive, risk-based approach to managing cyber and IT risks, with appropriate oversight by their boards and senior management.
Participants shared feedback on policy and operational matters concerning the NBFC sector.
(Brij Raj)                 Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1554

facts: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recordedMultiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities.
Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline.
Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday.

The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night.
Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches.
These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days.
Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento.
Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California.
By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday.

Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches.
These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days.
Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento.
Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California.
By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

facts: As part of the Reserve Bank’s ongoing engagement with regulated entities, the Governor, Reserve Bank of India, today met in Mumbai with the Managing Directors and Chief Executive Officers (MDs & CEOs) of select Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), including Government NBFCs, Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) and Microfinance Institutions.
Representatives of Sa-Dhan, the Micro Finance Institutions Network (MFIN) and the Finance Industry Development Council (FIDC) also participated.
Deputy Governors Shri Swaminathan J., Dr Poonam Gupta, Shri S.
Murmu and Shri Rohit Jain attended the meeting, along with other senior officers of the Reserve Bank.
The MD & CEO of the National Housing Bank also participated.
The Governor acknowledged the role of NBFCs and HFCs in supporting economic activity by widening access to credit.
He emphasised the need for responsible and sustainable credit growth and urged NBFCs to put customers first as they expand their business.
He highlighted the importance of quality service, effective grievance redressal and fair recovery practices.
He also encouraged NBFCs to use the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) for customer onboarding and to keep customer records in the registry up to date to improve customer convenience.

The Governor urged participants to strengthen their cybersecurity infrastructure and adopt a comprehensive, risk-based approach to managing cyber and IT risks, with appropriate oversight by their boards and senior management.
Participants shared feedback on policy and operational matters concerning the NBFC sector.
(Brij Raj)                 Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1554

GoI will have the option to retain additional subscription up to ₹2,000 crore against each security mentioned above.
The securities will be sold through Reserve Bank of India Mumbai Office, Fort, Mumbai–400001.
The sale will be subject to the terms and conditions spelt out in the ‘Specific Notification’ mentioned above and the General Notification F.No.4(2)–B(W&M)/2018, dated March 26, 2025.
The auction will be conducted using multiple price method.
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system) on November 27, 2026 (Friday).
The non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m.
and the competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m.
The result will be announced on the same day and payment by successful bidders will have to be made on November 30, 2026 (Monday).
Bids for underwriting of the Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) portion can be submitted by ‘Primary Dealers’ from 09:00 a.m.
up to 09:30 a.m.
on November 27, 2026 (Friday) on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading for a period commencing from November 25, 2026 – November 27, 2026.
Operational guidelines for Government of India dated securities auction and other details are given in the Annex.
Ajit Prasad                  Deputy General Manager      (Communications)          Press Release: 2026-2027/1551ANNEX      Type of Auction      1.
For multiple price-based auction, successful bids will get accepted at the respective quoted yield/price for the security.
For uniform price-based auction, bids will get accepted at the cut off yield/price accepted in the auction.
The auction will be yield based for new security and price based for securities which are re-issued.
In case of a Floating Rate Bonds (FRB), the auction will be spread-based for new security and price based for securities which are reissued.
At the time of placing bids for new FRB, the spread should be quoted in percentage terms.
Minimum Bid Size      4.
The securities will be issued for a minimum amount of ₹10,000/- (nominal) and in multiples of ₹10,000/- thereafter.
Non-Competitive Segment      5.

In all the auctions, Government security up to 5% of the notified amount for sale of individual security will be allotted to the eligible individuals and institutions under the Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility in the Auctions of Government Securities.
Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).

Each bank or Primary Dealer (PD) on the basis of firm orders received from their constituents will submit a single consolidated non-competitive bid for individual security on behalf of its constituents in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
Allotment under the non-competitive segment will be at the weighted average rate of yield/price of the successful bids that will emerge in the auction on the basis of the competitive bidding.
Submission of Bids      8.
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
Bids in physical form will not be accepted except in extraordinary circumstances.
Business Continuity Plan (BCP)-IT failure      10.
Only in the event of system failure, physical bids will be accepted.

Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office, Mumbai through (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form which can be obtained from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.
In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).
Multiple Bids      13.
An investor can submit more than one competitive bid in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
The aggregate amount of bids submitted by an investor in an auction should not exceed the notified amount of auction.
Decision Making Process      15.
On the basis of bids received, the Reserve Bank will determine the minimum price/maximum yield up to which tenders for purchase of Government Security will be accepted at the auctions.
Bids quoted at rates lower than the minimum price/higher than the maximum yield determined by the Reserve Bank of India will be rejected.
Reserve Bank of India will have the full discretion to accept or reject any or all bids either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.
Issue of Securities      18.

Issue of securities to the successful bidders will be by credit to Subsidiary General Ledger Account (SGL) or to Constituents’ Subsidiary General Ledger Account (CSGL), maintained with Reserve Bank of India.
Periodicity of Interest Payment      19.
Interest on the Government Security will generally be paid half-yearly other than in case of securities with non-standard maturities.
The exact periodicity of coupon payment is invariably mentioned in the specific notification for the issue of security.
Underwriting of the Government Securities      20.

The underwriting of the Government Securities under auctions by the ‘Primary Dealers’ will be as per the “Revised Scheme of Underwriting Commitment and Liquidity Support” announced by the Reserve Bank vide circular RBI/2007-08/186 dated November 14, 2007 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for Repurchase Transactions (Repo)      21.

The securities will be eligible for Repurchase Transactions (Repo) as per the conditions mentioned in Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Repurchase Transactions (Repo)) Directions, 2025 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for ‘When Issued’ Trading      22.

The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading in accordance with the guidelines on ‘When Issued transactions in Central Government Securities’ issued by the Reserve Bank of India vide circular No.
RBI/2018-19/25 dated July 24, 2018 as amended from time to time.
Investment by Non-Residents    23.

Investments by Non-Residents are subject to the guidelines on ‘Fully Accessible Route’ for Investment by Non-residents in Government Securities and other related guidelines as issued by the Reserve Bank from time to time.

facts: As part of the Reserve Bank’s ongoing engagement with regulated entities, the Governor, Reserve Bank of India, today met in Mumbai with the Managing Directors and Chief Executive Officers (MDs & CEOs) of select Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), including Government NBFCs, Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) and Microfinance Institutions.
Representatives of Sa-Dhan, the Micro Finance Institutions Network (MFIN) and the Finance Industry Development Council (FIDC) also participated.
Deputy Governors Shri Swaminathan J., Dr Poonam Gupta, Shri S.
Murmu and Shri Rohit Jain attended the meeting, along with other senior officers of the Reserve Bank.
The MD & CEO of the National Housing Bank also participated.
The Governor acknowledged the role of NBFCs and HFCs in supporting economic activity by widening access to credit.
He emphasised the need for responsible and sustainable credit growth and urged NBFCs to put customers first as they expand their business.
He highlighted the importance of quality service, effective grievance redressal and fair recovery practices.
He also encouraged NBFCs to use the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) for customer onboarding and to keep customer records in the registry up to date to improve customer convenience.

The Governor urged participants to strengthen their cybersecurity infrastructure and adopt a comprehensive, risk-based approach to managing cyber and IT risks, with appropriate oversight by their boards and senior management.
Participants shared feedback on policy and operational matters concerning the NBFC sector.
(Brij Raj)                 Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1554

facts: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recordedMultiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities.
Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline.
Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday.

The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night.
Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches.
These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days.
Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento.
Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California.
By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

facts: As part of the Reserve Bank’s ongoing engagement with regulated entities, the Governor, Reserve Bank of India, today met in Mumbai with the Managing Directors and Chief Executive Officers (MDs & CEOs) of select Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), including Government NBFCs, Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) and Microfinance Institutions.
Representatives of Sa-Dhan, the Micro Finance Institutions Network (MFIN) and the Finance Industry Development Council (FIDC) also participated.
Deputy Governors Shri Swaminathan J., Dr Poonam Gupta, Shri S.
Murmu and Shri Rohit Jain attended the meeting, along with other senior officers of the Reserve Bank.
The MD & CEO of the National Housing Bank also participated.
The Governor acknowledged the role of NBFCs and HFCs in supporting economic activity by widening access to credit.
He emphasised the need for responsible and sustainable credit growth and urged NBFCs to put customers first as they expand their business.
He highlighted the importance of quality service, effective grievance redressal and fair recovery practices.
He also encouraged NBFCs to use the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) for customer onboarding and to keep customer records in the registry up to date to improve customer convenience.

The Governor urged participants to strengthen their cybersecurity infrastructure and adopt a comprehensive, risk-based approach to managing cyber and IT risks, with appropriate oversight by their boards and senior management.
Participants shared feedback on policy and operational matters concerning the NBFC sector.
(Brij Raj)                 Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1554

facts: Today, the Reserve Bank released the November 2026 issue of its monthly Bulletin.
The Bulletin includes six speeches, four articles and current statistics.
The four articles are: I.
State of the Economy; II.
Shifting Drivers of Imported Inflation: COVID-19 Pandemic to the West Asia Conflict; III.
Performance of the NBFC Sector during 2025-26: A Review; and IV.
Disentangling the Impact of US Monetary Policy on Indian Financial Markets: An Event Study Approach.
State of the Economy  Supply side challenges, elevated energy prices, and geopolitical uncertainty remain significant headwinds to the global economic outlook.
Persistent inflationary pressures have led to synchronised monetary policy tightening across major central banks in the last three months.
Pullback in AI-related stocks and elevated sovereign bond yields, despite some softening from multi-decade highs, remain a source of volatility in financial markets.
Amidst uneven economic performance globally, the Indian economy stood out.
High-frequency indicators of domestic economic activity showed resilience in October, underpinned by strong credit demand.
Headline CPI inflation inched up, primarily driven by higher food inflation.
With strong exports performance, the trade deficit narrowed in October as compared to corresponding month of the previous year.
Equity markets rebounded supported by robust corporate earnings and foreign portfolio inflows.
Net inflows under ECB and NRI deposits also remained strong.
Shifting Drivers of Imported Inflation: COVID-19 Pandemic to the West Asia Conflict  By Snehal S.
Herwadkar, Ishu Thakur, Abhiruchi Rathi, Paras and Parul Arora  This article examines how successive global shocks have reshaped the drivers of imported inflation in India.
It constructs an import-intensity-weighted consumer price index (CPI) using item-level production, imports and exports data to assess the contribution of imported items to retail inflation.
The analysis finds that food and fuel were the principal channels through which imported inflation impacted retail inflation during the COVID-19 pandemic as also during the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Precious metals became a key source of imported core inflation from 2025, while the West Asia conflict renewed crude oil-related pressures in 2026.
Highlights:            The import-intensity-weighted measure indicates that imported items account for 8.5 per cent of the new CPI basket (base 2024=100).
Import intensity is highest for fuel and light, followed by food and beverages, and core components.
Despite the small weight of imported items in CPI basket, it contributed around 18 per cent to the CPI headline inflation in October 2026.
The West Asia conflict generated a sharper crude oil price shock than the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
However, the pass-through to retail fuel prices in the current episode has been relatively lower, limiting the pressures on imported inflation.
Higher precious metals prices emerged as another source of imported inflation since 2024.

Performance of the NBFC Sector during 2025-26: A Review  By Monalisa Poali, Pallavi Pant, Abhyuday Harsh and Brijesh P  This article assesses the performance of the non-banking financial company (NBFC) sector as at end-March 2026.
Highlights:            The NBFC sector continued to demonstrate double-digit y-o-y credit growth along with improvement in asset quality at end-March 2026.
